newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGAL PIN HOPES ON REPEAT TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGAL PIN HOPES ON REPEAT TRIUMPH.

text.p: Portugal, the only team to beat Germany in a World Cup qualifier, are desperate for history to repeat itself when they face the European champions on Saturday.
Despite heading qualifying group nine, the Portuguese can virtually wave goodbye to the World Cup finals if they lose.
The Portuguese, who beat Germany 1-0 away 11 years ago, have seven points, two more than Ukraine and three ahead of Germany, but they have played more games.
"It is very important...unless we win our situation is going to be very complicated," admitted Benfica striker Joao Vieira Pinto.
Coach Artur Jorge has recalled Porto's diminutive but highly experienced attacking midfielder Rui Barros to give pace to a side that has impressed but failed to score many goals.
"He is very fast and likes to get into the box," said Jorge about the one big change from the team that dominated Ukraine in a qualifying match in Oporto last month but still only won 1-0.

Portugal will also be without central defender Jorge Costa who has not played since Liberian striker George Weah broke his nose in an incident following a Porto-AC Milan European Champions' League game last month.
In contrast, Germany arrived in Portugal with a number of big names missing through injury or illness from their line-up.

But coach Berti Vogts said that the absence of top players, including midfielder Thomas Haessler and defenders Thomas Helmer and Thomas Strunz, would be no excuse if the Germans failed to improve on a poor display against unfancied Northern Ireland last month when they were held to a 1-1 home draw.
"The fact that players are missing is no excuse if we don't put on a decent show on Saturday. We don't have 'reserve' players," he said.
German confidence will be boosted by the return of libero Matthias Sammer, making his first appearance for the national side since the Euro 96 final last June.
"Matthias is very important for us," Vogts said. "With him we switch from defence to attack much more quickly."

Vogts' main dilemma is whether to replace Haessler with Werder Bremmen's gifted but erratic and often outspoken midfielder Mario Basler, or whether to push forward Bayern Munich winger back Christian Ziege into midfield.

Despite the selection problems, team captain Juergen Klinsmann was adamant that there would be nothing defensive about the German's approach on Saturday. "We aim to beat Portugal in their own stadium," he said.
Portugal - Vitor Baia, Carlos Secretario, Helder Cristovao, Fernando Couto, Dimas Teixeira, Oceano Cruz, Paulinho Santos, Rui Costa, Luis Figo, Joao Vieira Pinto, Rui Barros.
Germany - Andreas Koepke, Matthias Sammer, Juergen Kohler, Stefan Reuter, Markus Babbel, Dieter Eilts, Christian Ziege, Mario Basler, Andreas Moeller, Fredi Bobic, Juergen Klinsmann.
